overview.what_it_is: This lesson teaches how to measure and find angles. You will use a protractor and angle rules.

format_facts.label: Main skill
format_facts.value: Measure angles and work out missing angles.

format_facts.label: Measuring unit
format_facts.value: Angles are measured in degrees, shown by $^\circ$.

format_facts.label: Tools
format_facts.value: Use a protractor, ruler and sharp pencil.

scoring_factors.name: Correct rule
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether you chose the right angle total.

scoring_factors.name: Correct working
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether each subtraction step is shown clearly.

scoring_factors.name: Accurate measuring
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether the protractor was placed and read correctly.

scoring_factors.name: Degree sign
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether each angle answer includes the degree sign.

critical_rules: Angles on a straight line total $180^\circ$.
Always write $^\circ$ after an angle measurement.

learning_goals: You will measure an angle using a protractor.
You will choose the correct protractor scale.
You will spot vertically opposite angles.
You will use the straight-line rule.
You will use the angles-at-a-point rule.
You will find missing angles using subtraction.
You will work out turns on a compass rose.

core_method.name: Spot the Rule → Find the Total → Subtract
core_method.summary: First, study the diagram. Choose the angle rule. Subtract the known angles from the total.

steps.detail: Look for a square, straight line or full turn.
Decide which angle rule fits the diagram.
Write the correct total before doing any subtraction.
Take all known angles away from the total.
Add the angles and check the total.

core_method.formula: Right angle: $90^\circ$; straight line: $180^\circ$; around a point: $360^\circ$; vertically opposite angles: equal.

techniques.name: Place a protractor correctly
techniques.purpose: Measure an angle without shifting the starting point.
how_to: Put the centre mark on the angle point.
Line up the base with one angle arm.
Check that the arm begins at $0^\circ$.
Read where the other arm meets the scale.
Write the answer with the degree sign.
techniques.example: If the second arm meets $65^\circ$, the angle is $65^\circ$.
techniques.why_it_matters: A small placement error can change the answer.
techniques.common_error: Placing the centre mark beside the angle point.

techniques.name: Choose the correct scale
techniques.purpose: Avoid reading the matching number from the wrong row.
how_to: Find the arm lined up with the protractor base.
Start from the scale showing $0^\circ$ there.
Follow that scale towards the second arm.
Check whether the angle looks small or large.
techniques.example: An acute angle cannot measure $140^\circ$. Read $40^\circ$ instead.
techniques.why_it_matters: Most protractors show two number scales.
techniques.common_error: Reading $140^\circ$ for an angle that looks smaller than $90^\circ$.

techniques.name: Use vertically opposite angles
techniques.purpose: Find an angle without adding or subtracting.
how_to: Find two straight lines that cross.
Look directly across the crossing point.
Match the two opposite angles.
Copy the known angle measurement.
techniques.example: If one angle is $46^\circ$, its opposite angle is $46^\circ$.
techniques.why_it_matters: Opposite angles made by crossing lines are equal.
techniques.common_error: Matching two angles that sit beside each other.

techniques.name: Use a straight-line total
techniques.purpose: Find missing angles beside a straight line.
how_to: Check that the outer arms form one straight line.
Write the total as $180^\circ$.
Add the known angles when needed.
Subtract their total from $180^\circ$.
Check that all angles total $180^\circ$.
techniques.common_error: Using $360^\circ$ because the angles share one point.

techniques.name: Use angles around a point
techniques.purpose: Find a missing part of one full turn.
how_to: Check that the angles surround one point.
Write the full total as $360^\circ$.
Add all known angles.
Subtract their sum from $360^\circ$.
Check that every part totals $360^\circ$.
techniques.common_error: Forgetting one small angle in the diagram.

techniques.name: Use compass turns
techniques.purpose: Work out turns between compass directions.
how_to: Mark the starting direction.
Follow the stated turning direction.
Count each eighth-turn as $45^\circ$.
Add the equal turns together.
Stop at the final direction.
techniques.why_it_matters: Compass directions divide a turn into equal parts.
techniques.common_error: Turning clockwise when the question says counter-clockwise.

worked_examples.title: Measure an acute angle
worked_examples.input: A protractor is centred on an angle. One arm begins at $0^\circ$. The other arm meets $58^\circ$.
worked_examples.decoding: The angle begins on the correct zero mark. Read the same scale.
worked_examples.plan: Check the centre, base and starting scale. Then read the second arm.
worked_examples.model_answer: The centre mark is on the angle point. The base follows one arm. That arm begins at $0^\circ$. The other arm meets the scale at $58^\circ$. Therefore, the angle measures $58^\circ$.

annotations.part: The centre mark is on the angle point.
annotations.comment: This checks the protractor position.
This identifies the correct number scale.
The degree sign shows this is an angle.
The final answer is written as a sentence.

worked_examples.title: Find the missing part of a right angle
worked_examples.input: A right angle is split into $42^\circ$ and angle $p$. Find angle $p$.
worked_examples.decoding: The square corner shows a total of $90^\circ$.
worked_examples.model_answer: A right angle measures $90^\circ$. The known part is $42^\circ$. $p = 90^\circ - 42^\circ = 48^\circ$. Check: $42^\circ + 48^\circ = 90^\circ$. Therefore, angle $p$ is $48^\circ$.

annotations.comment: The square corner gives the total.
The known part is removed from the whole.
Adding both parts checks the answer.
The answer names the required angle.

worked_examples.title: Find an angle on a straight line
worked_examples.input: Angle $q$ and $37^\circ$ lie on one straight line. Find angle $q$.
worked_examples.decoding: The two angles form a half-turn of $180^\circ$.
worked_examples.model_answer: Angles on a straight line total $180^\circ$. The known angle is $37^\circ$. $q = 180^\circ - 37^\circ = 143^\circ$. Check: $37^\circ + 143^\circ = 180^\circ$. Therefore, angle $q$ is $143^\circ$.

annotations.comment: This is the total for a straight line.
Subtract the known part from the total.
The large answer fits the wide angle.
The check matches the straight-line total.

worked_examples.title: Find three angles on a straight line
worked_examples.input: Angles $35^\circ$, $DBE$ and $55^\circ$ lie on one straight line. Find angle $DBE$.
worked_examples.decoding: All three angles together must make $180^\circ$.
worked_examples.plan: Add the known angles. Subtract their total from $180^\circ$.
worked_examples.model_answer: Angles on a straight line total $180^\circ$. First add the known angles: $35^\circ + 55^\circ = 90^\circ$. Then find the missing angle: $\angle DBE = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ$. Check: $35^\circ + 90^\circ + 55^\circ = 180^\circ$. Therefore, angle $DBE$ is $90^\circ$.

annotations.comment: Combining known parts makes subtraction easier.
The known total is removed from the whole.
The missing angle is a right angle.
All three parts give the correct total.

worked_examples.title: Find an angle around a point
worked_examples.input: Angles around one point are $90^\circ$, $80^\circ$, $155^\circ$ and $x$. Find $x$.
worked_examples.decoding: The four angles make one full rotation of $360^\circ$.
worked_examples.plan: Add the three known angles. Subtract from $360^\circ$.
worked_examples.model_answer: Angles around one point total $360^\circ$. Add the known angles: $90^\circ + 80^\circ + 155^\circ = 325^\circ$. Find the missing angle: $x = 360^\circ - 325^\circ = 35^\circ$. Check: $90^\circ + 80^\circ + 155^\circ + 35^\circ = 360^\circ$. Therefore, angle $x$ is $35^\circ$.

annotations.comment: A full turn gives the total.
Every known angle is included.
The missing part completes the full turn.
The check confirms one full rotation.

worked_examples.title: Use vertically opposite angles
worked_examples.input: Two straight lines cross. Angle $w$ is $46^\circ$. Angle $x$ is directly opposite angle $w$. Find $x$.
worked_examples.decoding: The angles sit opposite each other across two crossing lines.
worked_examples.plan: Use the rule that vertically opposite angles are equal.
worked_examples.model_answer: Two straight lines cross at one point. Angles $w$ and $x$ are vertically opposite. Vertically opposite angles are equal. $x = 46^\circ$. Therefore, angle $x$ is $46^\circ$.

annotations.comment: The rule needs two crossing straight lines.
The angles are directly across the crossing.
No subtraction is needed.
The final answer clearly names the angle.

worked_examples.title: Find an interior angle
worked_examples.input: A straight line through point $O$ contains angles $105^\circ$, $COB$ and $50^\circ$. Find angle $COB$.
worked_examples.decoding: The three adjacent angles form one straight line.
worked_examples.plan: Add the known angles. Subtract their total from $180^\circ$.
worked_examples.model_answer: Angles on a straight line total $180^\circ$. Add the known angles: $105^\circ + 50^\circ = 155^\circ$. Find the missing angle: $\angle COB = 180^\circ - 155^\circ = 25^\circ$. Check: $105^\circ + 25^\circ + 50^\circ = 180^\circ$. Therefore, angle $COB$ is $25^\circ$.

annotations.comment: The two known parts are combined first.
The straight-line total is used.
The small answer matches the narrow space.
The check confirms the answer.

worked_examples.title: Turn clockwise on a compass rose
worked_examples.input: Start facing north. Turn clockwise until facing south-east. Find the turn.
worked_examples.decoding: Move from north through north-east and east to south-east.
worked_examples.plan: Count three equal eighth-turns. Each one measures $45^\circ$.
worked_examples.model_answer: North to north-east is $45^\circ$. North-east to east is another $45^\circ$. East to south-east is another $45^\circ$. The total turn is $45^\circ + 45^\circ + 45^\circ = 135^\circ$. Therefore, the clockwise turn is $135^\circ$.

annotations.comment: The direction of the turn must be followed.
Three compass gaps are crossed.
The three equal turns are added.
The answer includes the turning direction.

worked_examples.title: Correct a straight-line mistake
worked_examples.input: Ben says the missing angle beside $37^\circ$ is $323^\circ$ because $360^\circ - 37^\circ = 323^\circ$. Correct his work.
worked_examples.decoding: The angles lie on a straight line, not around a point.
worked_examples.plan: Replace the wrong total with $180^\circ$. Then subtract.
worked_examples.model_answer: Ben used the full-turn total by mistake. Angles on a straight line total $180^\circ$, not $360^\circ$. The correct working is $180^\circ - 37^\circ = 143^\circ$. Check: $37^\circ + 143^\circ = 180^\circ$. Therefore, the missing angle is $143^\circ$.

annotations.comment: A straight line is only half a full turn.
The correct total gives the correct answer.
The check proves the two angles form a line.
The corrected answer is stated clearly.

Use it to measure or draw an angle.

Line it up with one angle arm.
Read the row beginning at the correct zero.
Use it when a square marks $90^\circ$.
Use it when adjacent angles total $180^\circ$.
Use it when angles surround a point and total $360^\circ$.
Use it for equal angles across crossing lines.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using $360^\circ$ for angles on a straight line.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: A straight line is only half a full turn.
common_mistakes.fix: Use $180^\circ$ whenever the outer arms form one line.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The two scales give different angle measurements.
common_mistakes.fix: Start from the scale showing $0^\circ$ on the first arm.

common_mistakes.mistake: Placing the protractor away from the angle point.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The angle arms will meet the wrong scale marks.
common_mistakes.fix: Put the centre mark exactly on the angle point.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: Angles beside each other are not always equal.
common_mistakes.fix: Look directly across the crossing point.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The subtraction will use an incomplete known total.
common_mistakes.fix: Mark each known angle before adding them.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The answer looks like a plain number.

common_mistakes.mistake: Turning in the wrong compass direction.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: Clockwise and counter-clockwise may give different turns.
common_mistakes.fix: Draw a curved arrow before counting compass gaps.

common_mistakes.mistake: Trusting an answer that looks impossible.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: A small drawn angle should not have a very large measure.
common_mistakes.fix: Check whether the answer matches the angle size.

time_budget.focus: Place and read a protractor correctly.
Use opposite, straight-line and point rules.
Choose the rule without being told.
Check working, totals and degree signs.

drills.name: Protractor placement
drills.instructions: Place a protractor on six drawn angles. Do not measure yet.

drills.name: Measure and check
drills.instructions: Measure eight angles. Say whether each is small or large.

drills.name: Rule match
drills.instructions: Sort twelve diagrams into $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$, $360^\circ$ or equal.

drills.name: Straight-line gaps
drills.instructions: Find six missing angles on straight lines. Show each subtraction.

drills.name: Around-the-point gaps
drills.instructions: Find four missing angles around points. Include every known angle.

drills.name: Opposite pairs
drills.instructions: Mark equal opposite angles in five crossing-line diagrams.

drills.name: Compass turns
drills.instructions: Work out eight turns between compass directions.

drills.name: Error detective
drills.instructions: Correct four wrong answers. Name the wrong rule each time.

practice_plan.routine: Study the diagram first. Write the angle total. Show each step. Add all angles to check.

I can choose the correct protractor scale.
I can measure an angle in degrees.
I can spot a right angle.
I can identify vertically opposite angles.
I can use the $180^\circ$ straight-line rule.
I can use the $360^\circ$ full-turn rule.
I can find a missing angle using subtraction.
I can work out clockwise compass turns.
I can work out counter-clockwise compass turns.
I can check my answer by adding the angles.
I can write the degree sign correctly.
strategy_notes: Mark the total before writing any subtraction.
Use a small square as a clue for $90^\circ$.
Trace the outer arms to check for a straight line.
Circle the point when angles make a full turn.
Mark every known angle before adding them.
Estimate whether the missing angle looks small or large.
Check compass turns by counting $45^\circ$ gaps.
Finish by adding all parts back to the total.
